claim: Gli3 full-length can be methylated at K436 and K595.
source: Here we show that Gli3 full-length, but not the truncated form, can be methylated at K436 and K595.
evidence: Supported by mass spectrometry analysis and in vitro methylation assays shown in Figure 1.

claim: Gli3 methylation at K436 and K595 is specifically catalyzed by Set7.
source: This methylation is specifically catalyzed by Set7, a lysine methyltransferase (KMT).
evidence: Demonstrated through in vitro methylation assays with Set7 and immunoprecipitation experiments.

claim: Methylation at K436 increases the stability of Gli3.
source: Methylation at K436 and K595 respectively increases the stability and DNA binding ability of Gli3, resulting in an enhancement of Shh signaling activation.
evidence: Shown by cycloheximide chase experiments and western blot analysis in Figure 3.

claim: Methylation at K595 increases the DNA binding ability of Gli3.
source: Methylation at K436 and K595 respectively increases the stability and DNA binding ability of Gli3, resulting in an enhancement of Shh signaling activation.
evidence: Demonstrated by ChIP assays showing reduced DNA binding in Gli3K595R mutant.

claim: Gli3 methylation contributes to tumor growth and metastasis in non-small cell lung cancer in vitro and in vivo.
source: Furthermore, functional experiments indicate that the Gli3 methylation contributes to the tumor growth and metastasis in non-small cell lung cancer in vitro and in vivo.
evidence: Supported by MTT assays, soft agar assays, xenograft tumor models, and migration/invasion assays in Figure 4.

claim: Set7 mediated methylation is a novel PTM of Gli3 that positively regulates the transactivity of Gli3 and the activation of Shh signaling.
source: Therefore, we propose that Set7 mediated methylation is a novel PTM of Gli3, which positively regulates the transactivity of Gli3 and the activation of Shh signaling.
evidence: Supported by luciferase reporter assays and qPCR showing increased Shh target gene expression.

claim: Hedgehog signaling plays critical roles in embryonic development and tumor growth.
source: Hedgehog (Hh) signaling plays critical roles in embryonic development and tumor growth (Chen et al., 2007; Hooper and Scott, 2005; Ingham and McMahon, 2001; Nieuwenhuis and Hui, 2005; Yao and Chuang, 2015).
evidence: Supported by multiple literature citations.

claim: Misregulation of Hedgehog signaling leads to many types of cancers.
source: Its misregulation leads to many types of cancers (Gialmanidis et al., 2009; Hui and Angers, 2011; Jiang and Hui, 2008).
evidence: Supported by literature citations.

claim: Gli3 plays critical roles in modulating the switch-on and -off of Shh signaling.
source: Like Ci, Gli3 plays critical roles in modulating the switch-on and -off of Shh signaling.
evidence: Based on established scientific knowledge about Gli3 function.

claim: In the absence of Shh signaling, Gli3 is partially proteolyzed into a truncated transcriptional repressor (Gli3R).
source: In the absence of Shh signaling, Gli3 is partially proteolyzed into a truncated transcriptional repressor (Gli3R) to block the expression of downstream target genes.
evidence: Supported by literature citations (Dai et al., 1999; 2002).

claim: In the presence of Shh signaling, Gli3 is in a full-length transactivation form and activates the expression of downstream genes like Gli1 and Ptch1.
source: In the presence of Shh signaling, Gli3 is in a full-length transactivation form and activates the expression of downstream genes like Gli1 and Ptch1 (Dai et al., 1999; 2002).
evidence: Supported by literature citations.

claim: Post-translational modifications play important roles in regulating protein functions, especially in regulating the transactivity of transcriptional factors.
source: There is substantial evidence demonstrating that post-translational modifications (PTMs) play important roles in regulating protein functions, especially in regulating the transactivity of transcriptional factors (Filtz et al., 2014; Huang et al., 2013; Inuzuka et al., 2011; 2012; Liu et al., 2014; Munro et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by multiple literature citations.

claim: In the absence of Shh signal, Gli3 is phosphorylated by PKA, GSK3 and CKI, and subsequently ubiquitinated by SCFSlimb/β-TrcP for partial proteolyzation.
source: For example, in the absence of Shh signal, Gli3 is phosphorylated by PKA, GSK3 and CKI, and subsequently ubiquitinated by SCFSlimb/β-TrcP for partial proteolyzation to confer it trans-repressive activity (Chen et al., 2009; Hsia et al., 2015; Tempé et al., 2006; Wang et al., 2000; Wang and Li, 2006; Zhang et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by multiple literature citations.

claim: Protein methylation plays an important role in regulating the transduction of signaling pathways, like MAPK, BMP, WNT, Hippo and JAK-STAT.
source: Protein methylation is one of the most common PTMs and plays an important role in regulating the transduction of signaling pathways, like MAPK, BMP, WNT, Hippo and JAK-STAT (Bikkavilli and Malbon, 2012; Kim et al., 2013; Mazur et al., 2014; Oudhoff et al., 2013; Viña et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by multiple literature citations.

claim: Near 50 KMTs and 9 PRMTs had been identified in human genome.
source: So far, near 50 KMTs and 9 PRMTs had been identified in human genome (Biggar and Li, 2015).
evidence: Supported by literature citation.

claim: Set7 was first identified as a histone lysine methyltransferase specifically for Histone 3 lysine 4 monomethylation.
source: Although Set7 was first identified as a histone lysine methyltransferase specifically for Histone 3 lysine 4 monomethylation, an epigenetic marker associated with transcriptional activation (Nishioka et al., 2002; Wang et al., 2001), accumulating evidence indicates that methylation of non-histone proteins including P53, P65, TAF10 and so on is the major biological function of this enzyme (Biggar and Li, 2015; Chuikov et al., 2004; Ea and Baltimore, 2009; Yang et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by literature citations (Nishioka et al., 2002; Wang et al., 2001).

claim: Set7 mediated methylation of Lys372 in P53 increases its stability, resulting in the induction of P53 target genes.
source: Set7 mediated methylation of Lys372 in P53 increases its stability, resulting in the induction of P53 target genes (Chuikov et al., 2004).
evidence: Supported by literature citation.

claim: P65 can be methylated by Set7 at Lys37 which enhances the DNA binding and improves the expression of NF-κb target genes.
source: P65 can be methylated by Set7 at Lys37 which enhances the DNA binding and improves the expression of NF-κb target genes (Ea and Baltimore, 2009).
evidence: Supported by literature citation.

claim: Mass spectrometry analysis showed two methylation modifications on Gli3 K436 and K595 residues.
source: This mass spectrometry analysis showed two methylation modifications on Gli3 K436 and K595 residues (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Directly observed in mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The flanking sequences of K436 and K595 show strong similarities with reported Set7 substrates.
source: By comparing the flanking sequence of K436 and K595 with reported Set7 substrates, such as ERα (Subramanian et al., 2008), P53 (Chuikov et al., 2004), PCAF (Masatsugu and Yamamoto, 2009) and Histone 3 (Wang et al., 2001), we found strong similarities among them (Figure 1A, upper panel), suggesting the possible involvement of Set7 in methylation of these two residues.
evidence: Shown by sequence alignment in Figure 1A and supported by literature citations.

claim: Methylation signals were exclusively present in the Gli3 full-length but not the truncated repression form according to the mass spectrometry result.
source: Interestingly, these methylation signals were exclusively present in the Gli3 full-length but not the truncated repression form according to the mass spectrometry result (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Observed in mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: K436 and K595 sites in Gli3 are evolutionally conserved in many species.
source: Through sequence alignments, we found that these two sites in Gli3 are evolutionally conserved in many species (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Shown by sequence alignment in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: Set7 can specifically methylate the peptides, MBP-K436 and MBP-K595.
source: As shown in Figure 1B, Set7 can specifically methylate the peptides, MBP-K436 and MBP-K595, whereas the substitution of K436 or K595 with arginine (K436R or K595R) abolished Set7 mediated Gli3 methylation.
evidence: Demonstrated by in vitro methylation assay shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Substitution of K436 or K595 with arginine (K436R or K595R) abolished Set7 mediated Gli3 methylation.
source: As shown in Figure 1B, Set7 can specifically methylate the peptides, MBP-K436 and MBP-K595, whereas the substitution of K436 or K595 with arginine (K436R or K595R) abolished Set7 mediated Gli3 methylation.
evidence: Demonstrated by in vitro methylation assay shown in Figure 1B.

claim: GST pull-down assays indicated the interaction between Set7 and Gli3.
source: In addition, GST pull-down assays further indicated the interaction between Set7 and Gli3 (Figure 1C).
evidence: Shown by GST pull-down assay in Figure 1C.

claim: Only the full-length Gli3 contains the methylation signals on Gli3-K436 and Gli3-K595.
source: Consistent with the results of mass spectrometry, immunoprecipitation (IP) of endogenous Gli3 in HEK293T cells followed by immunoblot showed that only the full-length Gli3 contains the methylation signals on Gli3-K436 and Gli3-K595 (Figure 1D).
evidence: Demonstrated by immunoprecipitation and western blot in Figure 1D.

claim: The methylation signals on Gli3 were decreased upon Set7 knockdown.
source: The methylation signals were decreased upon Set7 knockdown, indicating that methylation on these two sites of Gli3 is mediated by Set7 (Figure 1D).
evidence: Shown by immunoprecipitation and western blot in Figure 1D.

claim: Overexpression of Set7 drastically improved the methylation levels whereas the catalytically inactive mutant of Set7, Set7H297A, had no effect on those methylations of Gli3.
source: Moreover, overexpression of Set7 drastically improved the methylation levels whereas the catalytically inactive mutant of Set7, Set7H297A (Wang et al., 2001), had no effect on those methylations of Gli3 (Figure 1E).
evidence: Demonstrated by immunoprecipitation and western blot in Figure 1E.

claim: Set7 failed to methylate Gli3K436R or Gli3K595R, the arginine substitution mutants of Gli3, in vivo.
source: Furthermore, Set7 failed to methylate Gli3K436R or Gli3K595R, the arginine substitution mutants of Gli3, in vivo (Figure 1F).
evidence: Shown by immunoprecipitation and western blot in Figure 1F.

claim: Cells with stable expression of Set7 shRNAs showed significantly reduced methylation signals on K436 and K595 of Gli3.
source: Cells with stable expression of individual unrelated Set7 shRNAs showed significantly reduced methylation signals on K436 and K595 of Gli3 compared to cells expressing luciferase control shRNA (Figure 1G).
evidence: Demonstrated by immunoprecipitation and western blot in Figure 1G.

claim: Gli3 arginine substitution mutants, Gli3K436R and Gli3K595R, showed abolished methylation signals when blotted with the matched antibodies.
source: Interestingly, like the Gli3WT, the protein levels of Gli3K595R were still subjected to the modulation of Set7, whereas the protein levels of Gli3K436R were not responding to either knockdown or overexpression of Set7 (Figure 3C and D).
evidence: Shown by western blot in Figure 1H.

claim: The methylation signals can be detected in Gli3PA but not in its arginine substitution mutants, Gli3PAK436R and Gli3PAK595R.
source: Similar to the result in Figure 1H, the methylation signals can be detected in Gli3PA but not in its arginine substitution mutants, Gli3PAK436R and Gli3PAK595R when blotted with respective antibodies (Figure 1I).
evidence: Shown by immunoprecipitation and western blot in Figure 1I.

claim: The methylation signals on Gli3 full length were only detected in embryonic lung tissues.
source: As shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4, the methylation signals on Gli3 full length were only detected in embryonic lung tissues.
evidence: Shown by western blot in Figure 1—figure supplement 4.

claim: GST-tagged Set7 can successfully pull down the flag-tagged Gli3 full-length of NIH-3T3 cells in the presence of Shh.
source: GST pull-down assays indicated that GST-tagged Set7 can successfully pull down the flag-tagged Gli3 full-length of NIH-3T3 cells in the presence of Shh (Figure 1J).
evidence: Shown by GST pull-down assay in Figure 1J.

claim: Set7 can methylate the full-length, but not the repression form of Gli3, at K436 and K595 residues.
source: Therefore, we demonstrate that Set7 can methylate the full-length, but not the repression form of Gli3, at K436 and K595 residues, indicating that Gli3 is a novel substrate of Set7.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from multiple experiments shown in Figure 1.

claim: In the absence of Shh, downregulation of Set7 had no effect on the luciferase activity.
source: In the absence of Shh, downregulation of Set7 had no effect on the luciferase activity.
evidence: Shown by luciferase reporter assay in Figure 2A.

claim: Set7 knockdown dramatically decreased the luciferase activity in the presence of Shh.
source: In contrast, Set7 knockdown dramatically decreased the luciferase activity in the presence of Shh, suggesting that Set7 plays a positive role on Shh pathway activation but has no effect on the basal level of Shh signaling (Figure 2A and A').
evidence: Shown by luciferase reporter assay in Figure 2A.

claim: Overexpression of Set7 but not its inactive mutant Set7H297A can significantly enhance the luciferase activity in the presence of Shh.
source: In line with this finding, overexpression of Set7 but not its inactive mutant Set7H297A can significantly enhance the luciferase activity in the presence of Shh (Figure 2B), suggesting that its methyltransferase activity is required for Set7 mediated Shh activation.
evidence: Shown by luciferase reporter assay in Figure 2B.

claim: Set7 mediated increase of luciferase activity was in a dose-dependent manner.
source: Furthermore, Set7 mediated increase of luciferase activity was in a dose-dependent manner (Figure 2C).
evidence: Shown by luciferase reporter assay in Figure 2C.

claim: NIH-3T3 cells expressing Set7 siRNAs showed significant reduction in Set7 protein levels and a parallel decrease in Gli1 and Ptch1 mRNA levels compared to cells expressing control siRNAs.
source: In the presence of Shh, NIH-3T3 cells expressing Set7 siRNAs showed significant reduction in Set7 protein levels and a parallel decrease in Gli1 and Ptch1 mRNA levels compared to cells expressing control siRNAs (Figure 2D–F).
evidence: Shown by qPCR and western blot in Figure 2D-F.

claim: Gli1 protein level was also decreased in cells with Set7 knockdown.
source: In addition, Gli1 protein level was also decrease in cells with Set7 knockdown (Figure 2F).
evidence: Shown by western blot in Figure 2F.

claim: Either Shh or SAG, the agonist of Shh pathway, directed activation of Shh signaling can upregulate Set7 levels.
source: It's of interest that either Shh or SAG, the agonist of Shh pathway, directed activation of Shh signaling can upregulate Set7 levels, whereas Gli1 knockdown can lead to a decrease of Set7 mRNA levels, suggesting the existence of a potential positive feedback loop between Set7 and Shh signaling (Figure 2A' and Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Shown by qPCR in Figure 2A' and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Gli1 knockdown can lead to a decrease of Set7 mRNA levels.
source: It's of interest that either Shh or SAG, the agonist of Shh pathway, directed activation of Shh signaling can upregulate Set7 levels, whereas Gli1 knockdown can lead to a decrease of Set7 mRNA levels, suggesting the existence of a potential positive feedback loop between Set7 and Shh signaling (Figure 2A' and Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Shown by qPCR in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: NIH-3T3 cells treated with Shh showed greatly increased methylation signals on Gli3.
source: In addition, NIH-3T3 cells treated with Shh showed greatly increased methylation signals on Gli3 which may be probably due to increased Gli3 full-length or/and Set7 levels (Figure 2A' and Figure 2—figure supplement 2), suggesting that the methylation signals of Gli3 is regulated by Shh input.
evidence: Shown by western blot analysis in Figure 2A' and Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: Set7 can positively regulate the activation of Shh signaling.
source: Taken together, these findings indicate that Set7 can positively regulate the activation of Shh signaling.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from multiple luciferase reporter assays and qPCR experiments.

claim: Set7 knockdown can suppress the activation of Shh signaling, but this inhibition was abolished when the Gli3 level was depleted by RNAi.
source: As shown in Figure 2G, although Set7 knockdown can suppress the activation of Shh signaling, this inhibition was abolished when the Gli3 level was depleted by RNAi.
evidence: Shown by luciferase reporter assay in Figure 2G.

claim: Depletion of both Gli1 and Gli2 in MEF cells showed no effect on releasing the inhibition due to Set7 knockdown.
source: In contrast, depletion of both Gli1 and Gli2 in MEF cells showed no effect on releasing such inhibition due to Set7 knockdown (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: Shown by qPCR in Figure 2—figure supplement 3.

claim: The mRNA levels of Gli1 and Ptch1 and the Shh luciferase activity were decreased in cells expressing Gli3K436R and Gli3K595R compared to Gli3WT.
source: Furthermore, compared to Gli3WT, the mRNA levels of Gli1 and Ptch1 and the Shh luciferase activity were decreased in cells expressing Gli3K436R and Gli3K595R, suggesting that Set7-directed Gli3 methylation plays an important role in maintaining Shh activation (Figure 2H–J).
evidence: Shown by qPCR and luciferase reporter assay in Figure 2H-J.

claim: Cells expressing the Gli3PA point mutants, Gli3PAK436R and Gli3PAK595R, showed decreased Shh luciferase activity and levels of Gli1 and Ptch1 transcripts compared to those with Gli3PAWT expression.
source: In consistent with this finding, cells expressing the Gli3PA point mutants, Gli3PAK436R and Gli3PAK595R, showed decreased Shh luciferase activity and levels of Gli1 and Ptch1 transcripts compared to those with Gli3PAWT expression (Figure 2—figure supplement 4).
evidence: Shown by qPCR and luciferase reporter assay in Figure 2—figure supplement 4.

claim: Either Set7 downregulation or upregulation can lead to the reduction or the induction of Shh luciferase activity respectively in cells with Gli3WT expression but not in cells expressing Gli3K436R and Gli3K595R.
source: Either Set7 downregulation or upregulation can lead to the reduction or the induction of Shh luciferase activity respectively in cells with Gli3WT expression but not in cells expressing Gli3K436R and Gli3K595R (Figure 2K and L).
evidence: Shown by luciferase reporter assay in Figure 2K and L.

claim: Gli3 methylation at K436 and K595 sites are required for Set7-mediated enhancement of Shh signaling activation.
source: Thus, our findings strongly suggested that Gli3 methylation at K436 and K595 sites are required for Set7-mediated enhancement of Shh signaling activation.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from multiple luciferase reporter assays.

claim: The Gli3 accumulation on the tips of cilia was comparable among cells with Set7 knockdown, Set7 overexpression, or Set7H297A overexpression.
source: As shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C and D, the Gli3 accumulation on the tips of cilia was comparable among those three groups, suggesting that the Set7-related changes of Shh activation are not due to the cilial translocation of Gli3.
evidence: Shown by immunofluorescence staining in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C and D.

claim: Knockdown of Set7 caused a significant reduction of endogenous Gli3 at protein levels.
source: Western blot showed that knockdown of Set7 caused a significant reduction of endogenous Gli3 at protein levels (Figure 3A, left panel), whereas overexpression of Set7 improved the Gli3 protein level (Figure 3A, right panel).
evidence: Shown by western blot in Figure 3A.

claim: Overexpression of Set7 improved the Gli3 protein level.
source: Western blot showed that knockdown of Set7 caused a significant reduction of endogenous Gli3 at protein levels (Figure 3A, left panel), whereas overexpression of Set7 improved the Gli3 protein level (Figure 3A, right panel).
evidence: Shown by western blot in Figure 3A.

claim: The mRNA level of Gli3 had no change regardless whether Set7 was knocked down or overexpressed.
source: This Set7 mediated induction of Gli3 seems due to PTMs, because the mRNA level of Gli3 had no change regardless whether Set7 was knocked down or overexpressed (Figure 3B).
evidence: Shown by qPCR in Figure 3B.

claim: The protein levels of Gli3K595R were still subjected to the modulation of Set7, whereas the protein levels of Gli3K436R were not responding to either knockdown or overexpression of Set7.
source: Interestingly, like the Gli3WT, the protein levels of Gli3K595R were still subjected to the modulation of Set7, whereas the protein levels of Gli3K436R were not responding to either knockdown or overexpression of Set7 (Figure 3C and D).
evidence: Shown by western blot in Figure 3C and D.

claim: The methylation at K436 but not K595 causes stability change of Gli3.
source: These findings suggested that the methylation at K436 but not K595 causes stability change of Gli3 (Figure 3C and D).
evidence: Inferred from western blot data in Figure 3C and D.

claim: The reduced half-life of Gli3K436R, but not Gli3WT or Gli3K595R was defined by western blot in cells treated with cycloheximide (CHX).
source: Finally, the reduced half-life of Gli3K436R, but not Gli3WT or Gli3K595R was defined by western blot in cells treated with cycloheximide (CHX) (Figure 3E and F).
evidence: Shown by western blot and quantification in Figure 3E and F.

claim: Set7 mediated methylation on K436 increases the protein stability of Gli3.
source: Therefore, these data indicated that Set7 mediated methylation on K436 increases the protein stability of Gli3.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from cycloheximide chase experiments.

claim: Knockdown of Set7 greatly decreased the binding of Gli3 on Gli1's promoter regions.
source: As shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2, knockdown of Set7 greatly decreased the binding of Gli3 on Gli1's promoter regions (Figure 3G and Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Shown by ChIP-qPCR in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: Set7 knockdown markedly affected the binding of Gli3 on Gli1's promoter regions.
source: ChIP assays with anti-flag antibody demonstrated that Set7 knockdown markedly affected the binding of Gli3 on Gli1's promoter regions (Figure 3G–I), suggesting that Set7 augments the DNA binding of Gli3 full-length.
evidence: Shown by ChIP-qPCR in Figure 3G-I.

claim: Gli3K595R-flag showed dramatically impaired DNA binding ability, whereas the Gli3K436R-flag presented the similar DNA binding ability to Gli3WT-flag.
source: ChIP assays with anti-flag antibody showed dramatically impaired the DNA binding ability in Gli3K595R-flag, whereas the Gli3K436R-flag presented the similar DNA binding ability to Gli3WT-flag (Figure 3K), suggesting that Set7 mediated methylation at K595 enhances the DNA binding ability of Gli3.
evidence: Shown by ChIP-qPCR in Figure 3K.

claim: Set7 mediated methylation at K595 enhances the DNA binding ability of Gli3.
source: ChIP assays with anti-flag antibody showed dramatically impaired the DNA binding ability in Gli3K595R-flag, whereas the Gli3K436R-flag presented the similar DNA binding ability to Gli3WT-flag (Figure 3K), suggesting that Set7 mediated methylation at K595 enhances the DNA binding ability of Gli3.
evidence: Inferred from ChIP-qPCR data in Figure 3K.

claim: The binding of Gli3 to Ptch1 and Hhip promoter regions was markedly impaired after Set7 knockdown.
source: As shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3, the binding of Gli3 to these regions was markedly impaired after Set7 knockdown.
evidence: Shown by ChIP-qPCR in Figure 3—figure supplement 3.

claim: Set7 improved the protein stability and DNA binding ability of Gli3 through methylation of K436 and K595 sites respectively.
source: In conclusion, Set7 improved the protein stability and DNA binding ability of Gli3 through methylation of K436 and K595 sites respectively.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from multiple experiments on protein stability and DNA binding.

claim: Both Set7 and Gli1 were extensively expressed in A549 cells.
source: By comparison on the mRNA levels of Set7 and Gli1 between Beas2B, a normal bronchial epithelial lung cell line, and A549, a non-small cell lung cancer cell line, we found that both Set7 and Gli1 were extensively expressed in A549 cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Shown by qPCR in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The GEO database search (GSE10245) showed a positive association between Set7 and Gli1 in NSCLC tumor samples.
source: Furthermore, the GEO database search (GSE10245) showed a positive association between Set7 and Gli1 in NSCLC tumor samples, suggesting the involvement of this Set7-Gli3-Gli1 axis in the development of NSCLCs (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: Shown by correlation analysis in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Depletion of Set7 displayed a decreased luciferase activity and reduced expression of Gli1 and Ptch1 in A549 cells.
source: Depletion of Set7 displayed a decreased luciferase activity and reduced expression of Gli1 and Ptch1 (Figure 4A and B).
evidence: Shown by luciferase reporter assay and qPCR in Figure 4A and B.

claim: Compared to A549 cells with stable Gli3WT expression, reduced luciferase activity and transcripts of Gli1 and Ptch1 were detected in cells stably expressing Gli3K436R, Gli3K595R or Gli3KRKR.
source: Compared to A549 cells with stable Gli3WT expression, reduced luciferase activity and transcripts of Gli1 and Ptch1 were detected in cells stably expressing Gli3K436R, Gli3K595R or Gli3KRKR (Figure 4C–E).
evidence: Shown by western blot, qPCR, and luciferase reporter assay in Figure 4C-E.

claim: More severe suppression on luciferase activities and Ptch1 mRNA, but not Gli1 mRNA, was observed in cells expressing Gli3KRKR.
source: In addition, more severe suppression on luciferase activities and Ptch1 mRNA, but not Gli1 mRNA, was observed in cells expressing Gli3KRKR, suggesting that the methylation at these two sites plays a synergistic role in regulating Shh signaling activation (Figure 4D and E).
evidence: Shown by qPCR and luciferase reporter assay in Figure 4D and E.

claim: MTT assays showed attenuated growth in cells stably expressing Gli3K436R, Gli3K595R or Gli3KRKR compared to cells with Gli3WT expression.
source: In line with the reduced Shh activation, MTT assays showed attenuated growth in cells stably expressing Gli3K436R, Gli3K595R or Gli3KRKR compared to cells with Gli3WT expression (Figure 4F).
evidence: Shown by MTT assay in Figure 4F.

claim: The ability to form colonies in soft agar was dramatically impaired in stable transfectants with the expression of Gli3K436R, Gli3K595R or Gli3KRKR compared to Gli3WT.
source: The ability to form colonies in soft agar was dramatically impaired in stable transfectants with the expression of Gli3K436R, Gli3K595R or Gli3KRKR compared to Gli3WT (Figure 4G and G').
evidence: Shown by soft agar assay in Figure 4G and G'.

claim: A549 cells with stable expression of Gli3K436R, Gli3K595R or Gli3KRKR showed retarded tumor growth in a xenograft tumor model.
source: In agreement with these in vitro growth assays, A549 cells with stable expression of Gli3K436R, Gli3K595R or Gli3KRKR showed retarded tumor growth in a xenograft tumor model (Figure 4H–J).
evidence: Shown by xenograft tumor experiments in Figure 4H-J.

claim: A549 cells with the expression of Gli3K436R, Gli3K595R or Gli3KRKR had limited migration ability compared to Gli3WT.
source: As shown in Figure 4K and L, A549 cells with the expression of Gli3K436R, Gli3K595R or Gli3KRKR had limited migration ability compared to Gli3WT.
evidence: Shown by wound healing and transwell migration assays in Figure 4K and L.

claim: The invasion ability of A549 cells stably expressing Gli3K436R, Gli3K595R or Gli3KRKR was substantially reduced.
source: Furthermore, matrigel chamber assays were performed and the invasion ability of A549 cells stably expressing Gli3K436R, Gli3K595R or Gli3KRKR was substantially reduced (Figure 4M).
evidence: Shown by matrigel invasion assay in Figure 4M.

claim: All the in vitro functional experiments in Figure 4 were repeated in A549 cells stably transfected with Gli3PAWT, Gli3PAK436R, Gli3PAK595R or Gli3PAKRKR, and showed similar results.
source: Moreover, all the in vitro functional experiments in Figure 4 were repeated in A549 cells stably transfected with Gli3PAWT, Gli3PAK436R, Gli3PAK595R or Gli3PAKRKR, and showed similar results (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Shown by multiple assays in Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: The methylation on Gli3 full-length regulates tumorigenesis in NSCLCs.
source: It further confirms that the methylation on Gli3 full-length regulates tumorigenesis in NSCLCs.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from experiments with Gli3PA mutants.

claim: Set7 can exclusively methylate Gli3 full-length at K436 and K595 sites in vitro and in vivo.
source: In present study, we demonstrated that Set7 can exclusively methylate Gli3 full-length at K436 and K595 sites in vitro and in vivo.
evidence: Summary of experimental findings from in vitro and in vivo methylation assays.

claim: These methylations on Gli3 augment the activation of Shh signaling.
source: These methylations on Gli3 augment the activation of Shh signaling.
evidence: Summary of luciferase reporter assays and qPCR experiments.

claim: Gli3 is a novel substrate of Set7.
source: To our knowledge, we for the first time identified Gli3 as a novel substrate of Set7 and demonstrated the involvement of Set7 in Shh activation.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from multiple experiments showing Set7-mediated Gli3 methylation.

claim: Set7 is involved in Shh activation.
source: To our knowledge, we for the first time identified Gli3 as a novel substrate of Set7 and demonstrated the involvement of Set7 in Shh activation.
evidence: Demonstrated by luciferase reporter assays and qPCR showing Set7's effect on Shh signaling.

claim: Set7 mediated methylation on K436 increases the protein stability of Gli3 whereas the methylation on K595 boosts the DNA binding of Gli3.
source: Furthermore, we showed that Set7 mediated methylation on K436 increases the protein stability of Gli3 whereas the methylation on K595 boosts the DNA binding of Gli3.
evidence: Demonstrated by cycloheximide chase experiments and ChIP assays.

claim: Set7-mediated Gli3 methylation contributes to the tumor growth and metastasis in NSCLCs in vitro and in vivo.
source: Finally, functional experiments indicated that this Set7-mediated Gli3 methylation contributes to the tumor growth and metastasis in NSCLCs in vitro and in vivo.
evidence: Demonstrated by MTT assays, soft agar assays, xenograft experiments, and migration/invasion assays.

claim: The PTMs of Gli3 like phosphorylation and ubiquitination are largely involved in determining the switch-off and -on of Shh signaling.
source: The PTMs of Gli3 like phosphorylation (Tempé et al., 2006; Wang et al., 2000; Wang and Li, 2006) and ubiquitination (Chen et al., 2009; Hsia et al., 2015; Zhang et al., 2009) are largely involved in this process.
evidence: Supported by multiple literature citations.

claim: Protein methylation participates in the regulation of signaling transduction of multiple signaling pathways, like MAPK, BMP, WNT, Hippo and JAK-STAT.
source: Protein methylation, as one of the most common PTMs, participates in the regulation of signaling transduction of multiple signaling pathways, like MAPK, BMP, WNT, Hippo and JAK-STAT (Bikkavilli and Malbon, 2012; Kim et al., 2013; Mazur et al., 2014; Oudhoff et al., 2013; Xu et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by multiple literature citations.

claim: Although Gli3R also has K436 and K595 residues, the Set7 mediated methylation solely occurs in Gli3 full-length.
source: It's of particular interest that, although Gli3R also has these two residues, K436 and K595, the Set7 mediated methylation solely occurs in Gli3 full-length.
evidence: Observed in mass spectrometry and western blot experiments.

claim: Lsd1 can possibly remove the methylation modifications of Gli3R.
source: Since Lsd1 is a nuclear protein, it is conceivable that Lsd1 can also remove the methylation modifications of Gli3R, resulting in these signals undetectable either by mass spectrometry or western blot.
evidence: Speculative reasoning based on Lsd1's known function and cellular localization.

claim: Increased Set7 could possibly compensate the demethylation effect of Lsd1 in the presence of Shh signaling.
source: Thus, in the presence of Shh signaling, although Gli3 full-length also translocates into the nucleus subjected to Lsd1 mediated demethylation, increased Set7 could possibly compensate this demethylation effect, resulting in augment in Shh signaling.
evidence: Speculative reasoning based on observed Set7 upregulation by Shh.

claim: The two methylation modifications of Gli3 at K436 and K595 are not redundant.
source: These two methylation modifications of Gli3 are not redundant, because arginine substitution in either point severely impairs the activation of Shh signaling, suggesting the role of Set7 in fine-tuning the transactivity of Gli3.
evidence: Inferred from experiments showing that mutation of either site impairs Shh signaling.

claim: Set7 can inhibit WNT signaling by methylating β-catenin.
source: Given that Set7 can inhibit WNT signaling by methylating β-catenin, and activate Shh signaling by methylating Gli3, it's very possible that Set7 is a key regulator involved in this WNT-Shh crosstalk.
evidence: Referenced as established knowledge in the discussion.

claim: Set7 is possibly a key regulator involved in WNT-Shh crosstalk.
source: Given that Set7 can inhibit WNT signaling by methylating β-catenin, and activate Shh signaling by methylating Gli3, it's very possible that Set7 is a key regulator involved in this WNT-Shh crosstalk.
evidence: Speculative reasoning based on Set7's effects on both WNT and Shh pathways.

claim: Abnormal activation of Shh signaling contributes to tumor development by promoting cell proliferation and EMT in many cancer types.
source: Abnormal activation of Shh signaling contributes to tumor development by promoting cell proliferation and EMT in many cancer types.
evidence: Based on established scientific knowledge about Shh signaling in cancer.

claim: Set7 mediated Gli3 methylation is critical for the oncogenic role of Shh pathway.
source: Our present study indicates that Set7 mediated Gli3 methylation is critical for this oncogenic role of Shh pathway because cancer cells expressing Gli3K436R, Gli3K595R or Gli3KRKR showed severely reduced growth and metastasis in xenograft tumor models.
evidence: Demonstrated by xenograft tumor experiments and in vitro functional assays.

claim: Set7 has therapeutic value in targeting Shh-dependent tumors, such as BCC, MB and Lung cancer.
source: This finding strongly suggests a therapeutic value of Ser7 in targeting Shh-dependent tumors, such as BCC, MB and Lung cancer.
evidence: Speculative conclusion based on experimental findings showing Set7's role in tumor growth.

claim: The activation of Shh pathway is required for epithelial to mesenchymal transition (EMT) in NSCLCs.
source: A recent report indicates that the activation of Shh pathway is required for epithelial to mesenchymal transition (EMT) in NSCLCs (Della Corte et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by literature citation.

claim: The stability of Dnmt1 can be dynamically regulated by Set7 and demethylase, Lsd1.
source: A recent study demonstrates that the stability of Dnmt1 can be dynamically regulated by Set7 and demethylase, Lsd1 (Wang et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by literature citation.

claim: There is a mutual repelling crosstalk between WNT and Shh pathways.
source: It has been recently reported that the activation of Shh signaling represses the canonical WNT signaling in colon epithelial cell differentiation, and that WNT pathway activation negatively regulates Shh pathway (van den Brink et al., 2004; Yanai et al., 2008), suggesting a mutual repelling crosstalk between these two pathways.
evidence: Supported by literature citations (van den Brink et al., 2004; Yanai et al., 2008).

claim: K595 is on the zinc finger which is important for DNA binding of Gli3.
source: Given that K595 is on the zinc finger which is important for DNA binding of Gli3 (Pavletich and Pabo, 1993), it's conceivable that the Set7 mediated methylation on K595 may contribute to increased DNA binding of Gli3.
evidence: Supported by literature citation (Pavletich and Pabo, 1993).

claim: Set7 can modulate the activation of multiple signaling pathways, such as NF-κb, JAK-STAT.
source: Set7 can modulate the activation of multiple signaling pathways, such as NF-κb, JAK-STAT, we sought to examine whether Set7 also regulates Shh signaling.
evidence: Referenced as established knowledge.

claim: The primary cilium (cilia) is an essential organelle for Shh signaling transduction in mammals.
source: In mammal, the primary cilium (cilia) is an essential organelle for Shh signaling transduction.
evidence: Based on established scientific knowledge.

claim: Gli3 traffics in and out of the cilia all the time.
source: Gli3 traffics in and out of the cilia all the time (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: Based on established knowledge and shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and B.

claim: In the presence of Shh, Gli3 initially accumulates in the cilium tip.
source: In the presence of Shh, Gli3 initially accumulates in the cilium tip (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B) and then functions as Gli3A to bind to the promoter of Gli1 to further transduce the signaling (Chen et al., 2009; Dai et al., 1999; 2002; Wen et al., 2010; Zhang et al., 2009).
evidence: Shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B and supported by literature citations.

claim: The Set7-related changes of Shh activation are not due to the cilial translocation of Gli3.
source: As shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C and D, the Gli3 accumulation on the tips of cilia was comparable among those three groups, suggesting that the Set7-related changes of Shh activation are not due to the cilial translocation of Gli3.
evidence: Inferred from immunofluorescence data in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C and D.

claim: Set7 has been reported to influence the stability of its methylated substrates like P53.
source: It has been reported that Set7 can influence the stability of its methylated substrates like P53 (Chuikov et al., 2004).
evidence: Supported by literature citation.

claim: Gli3 stability is important for Shh signaling activation.
source: Given the importance of Gli3 stability on Shh signaling activation (Tempé et al., 2006; Zhang et al., 2009), we then tested whether Set7 can also affect the stability of Gli3.
evidence: Supported by literature citations (Tempé et al., 2006; Zhang et al., 2009).

claim: Gli3 full-length is a transcription activator and can bind to the promoter of Gli1 to further enhance the activation of Shh signaling.
source: Gli3 full-length is a transcription activator and can bind to the promoter of Gli1 to further enhance the activation of Shh signaling (Hui and Angers, 2011; Jiang and Hui, 2008).
evidence: Supported by literature citations (Hui and Angers, 2011; Jiang and Hui, 2008).

claim: Set7 augments the DNA binding of Gli3 full-length.
source: ChIP assays with anti-flag antibody demonstrated that Set7 knockdown markedly affected the binding of Gli3 on Gli1's promoter regions (Figure 3G–I), suggesting that Set7 augments the DNA binding of Gli3 full-length.
evidence: Inferred from ChIP-qPCR data in Figure 3G-I.

claim: Misregulation of Shh pathway has been reported in many types of cancers, including basal cell carcinoma, medulloblastoma and lung cancer.
source: Misregulation of Shh pathway has been reported in many types of cancers, including basal cell carcinoma, medulloblastoma and lung cancer (Gialmanidis et al., 2009; Hui and Angers, 2011; Jiang and Hui, 2008; Yuan et al., 2007).
evidence: Supported by multiple literature citations.
